title: Extend runners-config schema with testing, evidence and environment tables
description:
Contract-first: this tick defines the shape every other tick in the epic consumes, so it runs alone in wave 1 and gets a foundation review.

Extend skills/ticks/references/runners-config.schema.json (and runners-config.md) with:
- [testing] — the commands implementers run, as a typed list. Keep an optional free-text notes field for the narrative hints (the Go/UI/worker caveats) so they do not have to leave the structured file to stay useful.
- [evidence] — closeout-only commands, explicitly separate from testing, preserving the existing rule that they may run ONLY during closeout.
- [evidence.acceptance] — the A<n> to command mapping, expressed as structure rather than prose. A schema gives uniqueness and typing directly, so the verbatim-and-uniquely-matching rules become validation instead of parsing heuristics. Keep the fail-closed SEMANTICS: an acceptance item mapped to an unknown, duplicated or absent command must fail, and nothing outside this file may authorise shell.
- [environment] — the pre-flight verification commands (test, do not ask).
- [orchestrator] — replace the Pi Orchestrator markdown block by mapping it onto the EXISTING roles and tiers vocabulary already in this schema. Do not invent a parallel set of keys; if a Pi-specific value has no home in the current shape, say so in the report rather than bolting on a second routing model.

Unknown keys must FAIL CLOSED, not be ignored: a typo silently degrading to no-warming or no-evidence is exactly the failure this epic exists to prevent. Validate every TOML example in runners-config.md against the schema (uv run --with jsonschema).

acceptance_criteria: The schema accepts a complete example covering all five tables and rejects: an unknown key, an acceptance item pointing at a command not defined in the file, a duplicate acceptance id, and an evidence command reused as a testing command; every TOML block in runners-config.md validates; no parallel routing vocabulary is introduced.
